It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment. This repository is maintained by Google DeepMind. MuJoCo has a C API and is intended for researchers and developers.

It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together. Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

items.title: Regulated firms can trial community bug-hunting skills inside their own AWS account
items.connection: SkillSpector scans the Claude-BugHunter bundle for prompt injection and supply-chain risk before install, and Bedrock AgentCore runs Claude Code with those skills in isolated sessions in the firm's own AWS account, returning findings as pull requests.
items.context: security teams usually block third-party agent extensions that run with real access
chain: Claude-BugHunter packages 82 skills and 681 disclosed-report patterns across 24 core vulnerability classes.
Security teams normally reject such a bundle because skills run with real access and come from unknown authors.
A pre-install scan plus isolated sessions in the firm's own cloud answers both the supply-chain and the data location objections.
Findings arrive as GitHub pull requests, so they enter the existing review queue instead of a new tool.
items.who: Internal application security teams at banks, insurers and healthcare firms benefit; the security budget pays for AWS compute.
items.variable: Time from finding a useful skill bundle to approved internal use
items.versus: Installing the bundle on laptops fails security review, and commercial scanners do not encode disclosed-report patterns.
items.smallest_test: Scan the bundle with SkillSpector, then run it in AgentCore on a repo with known past vulnerabilities; success if the scan raises no blocking issues and the run rediscovers issues the current scanner missed.
items.disconfirm: SkillSpector flags much of the bundle, or most pull requests from the run are false positives.

items.title: Clinical AI vendors can rank models by wrong findings, not only coverage
items.connection: The Sante report separates full-credit coverage from incorrect required findings, and SkillEvaluator's synthetic datasets and live behavior measurements let a team apply that split to every change in its own clinical skills.
items.context: health systems ask vendors for safety evidence before procurement
chain: Sante matched DeepSeek on coverage across 18 cardiac-risk questions but had 38 percent fewer incorrect required findings than DeepSeek plus Kimi, so models with equal coverage can differ on errors.
A team adopts that split as its scoring rule and uses SkillEvaluator to build synthetic cases and measure live agent behavior for each skill version.
A skill change that raises coverage but adds wrong findings is stopped at a quality gate instead of shipping.
Procurement packets can report errors by clinical skill, which gives hospital safety committees a concrete basis for review.
items.who: Clinical decision support startups benefit and pay in engineering time; hospital safety and procurement teams gain clearer evidence.
items.versus: Coverage-only leaderboards hide the error type that matters clinically, and doing nothing leaves skill edits untested.
items.smallest_test: Rebuild the 18 cardiac-risk question format as a SkillEvaluator dataset and score two skill versions; success if the incorrect-findings metric changes the ranking that coverage alone would give.
items.disconfirm: Coverage and incorrect findings move together across every skill change, so the second metric never changes a decision.

items.title: Planners can fix hard statement layouts by having agents read page images
items.connection: On 2026-11-15 Magpie suggested financial planners turn client statement PDFs into agent-maintained Univer spreadsheets through a document converter; today Qwen4-Max adds native vision with a 1 million token context, so layouts that break text conversion can be read from page images and cross-checked before values land in Univer.
items.context: client financial data often cannot go to unvetted third-party APIs
chain: The earlier idea's weak point was parsing errors on hard statement layouts.
Qwen4-Max can read the statement pages as images and hold a client's full statement history in one context.
The agent writes values into a Univer sheet and flags cells where the image reading and the converted text disagree.
Planners review only flagged cells, so onboarding a client's history becomes review instead of data entry.
items.who: Independent planners and small advisory firms benefit; they or planning software vendors pay.
items.variable: Planner minutes per new client onboarding
items.versus: Typing numbers is slow, and text-only conversion fails on exactly the statements that cost planners the most time.
items.smallest_test: Take statements whose layouts broke the converter; success if image plus text cross-checking produces fewer wrong cells than the converter alone and flags most of the errors that remain.
items.disconfirm: Disagreement flags fire on most cells, so planners still check everything, or compliance blocks the hosted API.

items.title: Strict agent approval gates stop stalling work when leads can approve from phones
items.connection: LoopForge adds human approval gates to self-hosted coding-agent workflows, and T3code lets the approver reach the Claude Code and Codex sessions behind those gates from a phone.
items.context: approvers spend much of the day in meetings or away from their desks
chain: LoopForge puts explicit human approvals between agent steps in a delivery workflow.
Each gate costs wall-clock time whenever the approver is away from the machine running the agent.
T3code lets that approver inspect and steer the Claude Code or Codex session from a phone, so the next step can start sooner.
Teams can keep stricter gates without idle agents, which makes gated agent work acceptable to cautious managers.
items.who: Engineering leads at teams running self-hosted agents benefit; the platform team pays the setup time.
items.variable: Median gate wait time per agent task
items.versus: Without remote access teams either loosen gates or accept idle agents, and hosted alternatives often require code to leave the network.
items.smallest_test: For a sprint, route gated LoopForge tasks through sessions reachable with T3code; success if median gate wait falls against the previous sprint with no rise in reverted merges.
items.disconfirm: Approvers refuse to review diffs on a phone and wait for a laptop anyway, or the gates do not surface in the sessions T3code reaches.
